**Wire verb `library calibrate-rt`**: Fit each run's map from retention time in minutes onto a spectral library's iRT scale from anchors you choose, and convert the times you send with them, in either direction.

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stdin` (wire `--stdin`) | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 anchor line; optionally a '--' line and query lines` | Two lists of tab-separated lines, group, rt\_minutes, irt, split by one line holding only '--' (BULK.md section 2). No header; blank lines are skipped; a UTF-8 BOM is dropped. ANCHORS come first: one (observed retention time in minutes, library iRT) pair per line; mzLib asks for the observed apex time of confidently identified precursors (IrtCalibration.cs:29-31), and which ones is the caller's choice. A blank, NA or NaN anchor value reaches mzLib as NaN, which it refuses. QUERIES follow the '--', if any: each gives exactly one of rt\_minutes (convert to iRT, IrtCalibrationModel.ToIrt) or irt (convert to minutes, ToRtMinutes) and leaves the other blank. group is any non-empty name, typically the run; each group is fitted by its own IrtCalibration.Fit call on its own anchors, and its queries are converted by that fit. Groups are reported in order of first appearance, over both lists. |
| `kind` (wire `--kind`) | `string` | `lowess` | — | `linear \| lowess` | IrtCalibrationOptions.Kind. lowess (mzLib's default) is a robust locally weighted regression for a gradient that bends; linear is one straight line, fitted robustly. Absent sends nothing, so mzLib's default applies. |
| `minimum_anchors` (wire `--minimum-anchors`) | `int` | `20` | anchors | `>= 3 (mzLib's own check)` | IrtCalibrationOptions.MinimumAnchors: a group with fewer anchors is refused rather than fitted. Absent means mzLib's default, 20 at the pin; the bridge sends no number of its own. |
| `bandwidth` (wire `--bandwidth`) | `float` | `0.3` | fraction of anchors | `(0, 1] (mzLib's own check)` | IrtCalibrationOptions.Bandwidth, LOWESS only: the share of a group's anchors in each local fit (at least 3). Smaller follows the gradient more closely and noise too. Absent means mzLib's default, 0.3 at the pin. mzLib checks it for linear too, and does not use it there. |
| `knots` (wire `--knots`) | `int` | `100` | points | `>= 3 (mzLib's own check)` | IrtCalibrationOptions.Knots, LOWESS only: how many evenly spaced times between the first and last anchor the curve is fitted at; between them it is a straight line. Absent means mzLib's default, 100 at the pin. |
| `robustness_iterations` (wire `--robustness-iterations`) | `int` | `3` | iterations | `>= 0 (mzLib's own check)` | IrtCalibrationOptions.RobustnessIterations: rounds of Tukey bisquare reweighting after the first fit, each downweighting anchors with large residuals. 0 keeps the first fit, which is already weighted from binned medians. Absent means mzLib's default, 3 at the pin. |
| `on_error` (wire `--on-error`) | `string` | `fail` | — | `fail \| skip` | fail: the first group mzLib refuses (too few anchors, a non-finite one, anchors at one time only, or iRT that does not increase with time) stops the call with a usage error naming the group. skip: that group's error is set, its rows carry the times given and null for the rest, and the other groups are fitted. An option mzLib refuses fails the call either way. |

# Errors

| Kind | mzLibRust returns | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | kind given without a value or not linear or lowess; minimum-anchors, knots or robustness-iterations not an integer; bandwidth not a number; any of them given without a value; on-error not fail or skip |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | stdin has no anchor line; a line with other than 3 tab-separated fields; an empty group; a value that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a second '--' line; a query with both rt\_minutes and irt, or with neither; a query value that is not finite |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | mzLib refuses an option (IrtCalibrationOptions out of range: MinimumAnchors below 3, Bandwidth outside (0, 1\], Knots below 3, RobustnessIterations below 0; mzLib's ArgumentOutOfRangeException, reclassified), whatever on-error says |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | with on-error fail, mzLib refuses a group's anchors: fewer than minimum\_anchors (a group with queries and no anchors included), a non-finite value, all at one time, or a fit whose iRT does not increase with time (mzLib's ArgumentException, reclassified); the message starts with the group |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | never expected |
| `service_unavailable` | [`MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable`](crate::MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable) | never returned by this verb |

Any call can also fail on the way to mzLib or back, whatever the verb: [`MzLibError::BridgeNotFound`](crate::MzLibError::BridgeNotFound), [`MzLibError::Timeout`](crate::MzLibError::Timeout), [`MzLibError::Protocol`](crate::MzLibError::Protocol) or [`MzLibError::Io`](crate::MzLibError::Io).

# Caveats

- iRT is the scale of the library the anchors' iRT values came from. A calibration maps one run onto that library's scale, so iRT values from two libraries are not comparable, and the same run calibrated against two libraries gives two maps.
- The anchors are the caller's choice: mzLib asks for the observed apex retention time, in minutes, of confidently identified precursors paired with their library iRT (IrtCalibration.cs:29-31). The bridge applies no q-value cutoff and removes no duplicate. The fit is robust to some wrong anchors (binned medians, then Tukey bisquare reweighting), not to a wrong choice of them.
- residual\_sd is mzLib's robust residual SD, in iRT units, of the anchors that fit: residuals beyond 3 robust SDs are set aside before it is computed (IrtCalibration.InlierSd). It understates the spread when many anchors are wrong, and a LOWESS fit to few anchors can pass through nearly all of them, so a residual\_sd near 0 there means an overfit, not a perfect run. irt minus fitted\_irt on the anchor rows shows every residual.
- Outside each group's first and last anchor the map continues as a straight line, not a fit (IrtCalibrationModel.IsExtrapolated). Read is\_extrapolated before trusting a converted time there.
- The fitted curve itself does not cross the wire: mzLib keeps its knots private and its constructor internal (IrtCalibrationModel), so a calibration cannot be returned and reused. Send the queries in the same call as their anchors; refitting the same anchors gives the same map, because mzLib sorts them first.
